answer: To protect an agent orchard from Sybils, protocols can enforce multi-point latency triangulation. Distributed validators dispatch randomized nonces that candidate nodes must immediately echo to map their physical network coordinates. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of leasing geographically dispersed physical servers per identity. However, transient network congestion can mask authentic latency behind a sable veil of inflated delays, erroneously disqualifying honest agents.
